text:
Hi everyone,

I am currently completing the Nativ application, and the system shows the following list of recommended documents:

•⁠  ⁠Original birth certificates of all family members

•⁠  ⁠Documents confirming the marital status of all family members

•⁠  ⁠Parents’ marriage certificate

•⁠  ⁠Original birth certificates of the parents

•⁠  ⁠Documents and certificates belonging to grandparents

•⁠  ⁠Death certificates

•⁠  ⁠Employment record books

•⁠  ⁠Military service documents

•⁠  ⁠Documents confirming the education of family members

•⁠  ⁠Police clearance certificates for all family members over the age of 14, with an apostille and issued within the last six months

•⁠  ⁠Any other documents proving eligibility under the Law of Return

Does anyone know whether we really need to upload all of these documents, or only the ones that exist and are relevant to the applicant? Or just skip this ridiculously unnecessary step? If I don't have children and have never been married.

Also, do we need to present all the original documents during the interview with Nativ?

Thank you!
